quote: given an undertaking to
why: "Promised" or "undertaken" is the buried verb.

quote: carry out an assessment of
why: "Assess" says the same with the verb restored.

quote: made the decision to
why: "Decided" says the same in one word.

quote: Since the election
why: "Election" names an event, not a buried action.

quote: Flood warnings for Quay Street were not issued until after six
why: A reported piece should say which agency issued the warnings late.

quote: Sandbags had been promised to businesses
why: The passive hides who made the promise that was broken.

quote: The street was closed by police at seven.
why: The actor is stated.

quote: The flood wall was built in 1962
why: Who built the wall is irrelevant to the point.

quote: She carried the cash box and the order book up to the flat above the shop. She went back for a tray of sourdough starter that she has kept alive since 1998. She left
why: Four consecutive sentences open with "She".

quote: In the weeks after the water went down and the loss adjuster had come round to photograph each and every room, Ellen
why: Twenty-one words of introductory phrase come before the subject.

quote: really extensive
why: "Really" adds emphasis; the next sentence gives the facts.

quote: It was obviously a shock
why: "Obviously" adds nothing.

quote: very small
why: "Very" intensifies without a fact.

quote: only one oven works
why: "Only" states a limit and carries meaning.

quote: has never missed a Christmas order
why: "Never" is the claim itself.

quote: sodden flour stayed in the building for weeks. Tom pulled out the sodden
why: An uncommon word appears in two consecutive sentences for no reason.

quote: each and every
why: A doubled pair where one word does the work of both.

quote: an assessment of the flood wall
why: "Flood wall" names a structure and must repeat exactly.

quote: The bakery is the beating heart of Quay Street, and when a heart stops, the whole body feels it.
why: Stock imagery stands in for saying what the bakery's closure did to the street.

quote: A wave of support followed that lit a fire under the council.
why: Water and fire figures contradict each other, and neither says what the support was.

quote: the flood was a wake-up call
why: A stock phrase that carries no information.

quote: The river had broken its banks in the night.
why: A dead metaphor that is the literal description of a flood.

quote: The insurance payment, when it came in August
why: The payout arrives before the reader knows about the damage; it belongs near the reopening.

quote: Gluten development depends on water temperature
why: The sentence opens on unfamiliar material with no link to the flour run before it or the sales after it.

quote: It is difficult to overstate how much the flood affected the people of the street
why: The paragraph restates the effect of the flood in general terms and adds no fact.
